attacked.target: The receipt is classified as income from other sources, recognized on the date of credit (28 June 2026), valued using the telegraphic transfer buying rate on the last day of the tax year (31 March 2027), and is subject to TDS at 1% if the threshold is exceeded. The penalty position is governed by s.439(8), requiring a bona fide explanation and disclosure of all material facts.
attacked.attack: The provision cited, Rule 56, Income-tax Rules, 2026, does not directly address the classification of income from other sources or the recognition date. Additionally, the valuation method using the telegraphic transfer buying rate on the last day of the tax year is prescribed by Rule 206, not Rule 56. Therefore, the citation of Rule 56 is incorrect for these aspects.
attacked.evidence: Rule 56, Income-tax Rules, 2026, states: 'For the purposes of this rule and rule 57,— ... (i) "valuation date" means the date provided in the Table below:' This rule does not cover the classification of income or the recognition date. Rule 206, Income-tax Rules, 2026, states: '(1) The rate of exchange for the calculation of the value in rupees of any income...shall be the telegraphic transfer buying rate of such currency as on the specified date.' This rule should be cited for the valuation method.
